title: Zelensky Speaks with Trump, Calls for Lasting Peace: 'Not Just Another Pause Between Russian Invasions'
detail: On May 27, 2026 (Day 1,553 of Russia's full-scale invasion), President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with US President Donald Trump and afterward posted on X (formerly Twitter): 'A real peace must be achieved, one that will be lasting, not just another pause between Russian invasions. Killings must stop as soon as [possible].' The statement reflects Ukraine's insistence that any ceasefire or peace agreement must include robust security guarantees — not merely a suspension of hostilities that Russia could use to rearm and reinvade. The diplomatic track remains stalled after the February 2026 Geneva talks collapsed after just two hours on the second day. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed in mid-May that peace negotiations are currently not underway. Zelensky has also been invited to the upcoming NATO summit in Ankara, confirmed by NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

media.caption: Zelensky speaks with Trump on May 27 and calls for 'real, lasting peace — not just another pause between Russian invasions'

title: Zelensky Denies Planning 2-3 More Years of War — Actual Focus Is on Next Six Months, Up to November 2026
detail: On May 27, 2026, Zelensky's office denied media reports that he had instructed Ukrainian officials to plan for another 2-3 years of active war. His actual message to parliament focused on the next six months — through November 2026 — as the critical window for diplomatic progress. The clarification came amid intense international pressure for a ceasefire following Russia's May 24 mass attack on Kyiv (600 Shahed drones + 90 missiles + Oreshnik hypersonic ballistic missile), which killed 4 and injured 80+. Zelensky simultaneously maintained Ukraine's position that any peace deal must include iron-clad security guarantees to prevent Russia from using a ceasefire to rearm and reinvade. Ukraine has been invited to the NATO Ankara summit (confirmed by NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte), a significant step toward the institutional security architecture Ukraine is seeking.

media.caption: Zelensky denies planning 2-3 more years of war — focus is on next 6 months (through November 2026) for diplomatic resolution

title: Zelensky Warns Belarus of 'Consequences' If It Deepens Involvement in War Against Ukraine
detail: On May 26, 2026, President Zelensky warned Belarus that Ukraine was prepared to take 'preventive measures' and would impose 'consequences' if Belarus were to play a greater role in Russia's war against Ukraine. The warning reflects concerns that Russian pressure on Lukashenko — whose country hosted Russian forces for the February 2022 invasion axis through Chernobyl toward Kyiv — could result in a more active Belarusian military role. Belarus has allowed Russian forces to station Wagner Group units on its territory following the 2023 Wagner mutiny, and Russian nuclear weapons were deployed to Belarus in 2023. Ukraine has maintained open dialogue with Belarusian democratic opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, with Zelensky hosting her in Kyiv in May 2026 in her first official visit there. The warning underscores the sensitivity of Belarus's position as a potential staging ground for a second northern front.

media.caption: Zelensky warns Belarus of consequences if it plays greater role in Russia's war — Ukraine prepared to take preventive measures (May 26, 2026)
